summary.text: Water vapor feedback is a physical climate feedback in which a warmer atmosphere comes to hold more water vapor.
Because water vapor is a greenhouse gas, the extra vapor warms the atmosphere further, which lets it hold still more water vapor.
It is also called the specific humidity feedback, since relative humidity stays nearly constant over the oceans but falls over land, which warms faster.

facts.label: Kind of feedback
facts.value: Physical, alongside reduced snow and ice cover

items.prompt: The atmosphere warms by a couple of degrees. What happens to the total amount of water vapor it holds?

options.label: It rises, since warm air can hold more
It falls, since heat breaks vapor apart
It stays fixed by the size of the oceans
It falls, since more of it turns to rain

items.explain: Saturation vapor pressure is higher in warmer air, so the absolute amount of water vapor increases as the atmosphere warms.

items.prompt: Warming adds water vapor to the air. What does that extra vapor then do to the warming?

options.label: Cancels it by making the air heavier
Has no effect, since vapor traps no heat
Reverses it by blocking the sunlight
Adds to it by trapping more heat

items.explain: Water vapor is a greenhouse gas, so more of it warms the atmosphere further, letting it hold still more vapor.

items.prompt: Scientists call water vapor feedback a positive feedback. What does that label tell you?

options.label: It is good for the planet
It amplifies the starting change
It has been measured precisely
It is caused only by people

items.explain: A positive feedback amplifies an initial change; the name says nothing about whether it is good or bad.

items.prompt: Relative humidity stays nearly steady over the oceans but has dropped over land. Why the difference?

options.label: Land has more clouds blocking the sunlight
Oceans are warming much faster than land
Land is warming faster than the oceans
Rain now falls only over the land

items.explain: Land experiences faster warming than the ocean, and relative humidity over land has declined.

items.prompt: More warmth brings more vapor, which brings more warmth. What keeps this from turning into a runaway greenhouse effect on Earth?

options.label: A warmer planet sheds more heat as radiation
Water vapor stops trapping heat when hot
The oceans will soon run out of water
Extra clouds always block all extra sunlight

items.explain: Thermal radiation rises as the planet warms, an effect several times larger than any other single feedback, so net feedbacks stay negative and human-caused change alone cannot cause a runaway.

items.prompt: Water vapor feedback is a physical feedback, not a partly biological one. Which other effect belongs in the same physical group?

options.label: Plants taking up CO₂ at a changing rate
Shrinking snow and ice reflecting less light
Forests storing carbon as they grow larger
Oceans and plants soaking up CO₂ emissions

items.explain: Physical feedbacks include reduced reflectivity from shrinking snow and ice and added water vapor, while biological ones involve plants taking up CO₂.
